title.narrative: Fostered cooperative and social and solidarity economy and enhanced productivity and resilience in key supply chains

description.narrative: Cooperatives and enterprises in the Occupied Palestinian Territory (OPT) offer a unique avenue for increased productivity and enhanced economic resilience through models of Social Solidarity Economy (SSE), particularly in times of crisis. That said, cooperatives and enterprises in OPT often work in an informal way and face a unique set of challenges that limit their capacity to offer this socio-economic contribution, challenges that are only exacerbated in times of economic crisis. In line with priorities identified in the National Employment Strategy (NES), the ILO will implement a range of interventions to promote decent work in the cooperatives and Small and Medium Enterprises (SME) sectors, through entrepreneurship and cooperative development utilizing ILO tools adapted to the local context. Interventions of the ILO in OPT will range from policy-level support and capacity building to government agencies regulating these sectors, to primary-level support targeting entrepreneurs and primary cooperatives. In support of the agriculture sector in OPT, the ILO has launched various interventions that aim to advance the capacities of cooperatives and small-scale producers to improve production while incorporating decent work principles and practices. These interventions were designed following a comprehensive value chain analysis led by the ILO that identified constraints to productivity and decent work in the Dairy and Honey sub-sectors. The ILO will build and expand on this support, to offer more direct support to primary cooperatives in areas of management, productivity and access to markets. This is expected to allow for more streamlined operations as well as promote business-to-business linkages. Furthermore, the ILO will support the formalization of small-scale farmers to work within entrepreneurial and cooperative SSE models and will support the establishment of new cooperatives under innovative models.
